title: Business Judgment Specification — draft 0.1.0
description: Piece 3 of the growth layer: what a fact means under a rule (the judgment specification defines business meaning — terms, units, evidence sources, time windows, boundaries, precedence, coverage and exception behavior; unknown/unresolved is distinct from refusal unless an authorized specification defines otherwise — overall-design §2; fixture conventions — proposal §10; P4: neither may grant itself permission). Every field below carries its own provenance anchor — nothing is invented here. A semantic classification is not proof of authority: this schema says nothing about permissions (the principle sentence lives in the legacy overall-design §6; the current proposal does not re-state it — see the drift register in schema/README.md). Provenance (dual anchor): semantics per the current overall-design §2/P4/P5 and proposal §5/§10; formerly NGA overall-design §6/§6.1 (superseded by the 2026-10-31 consolidation). 'Proposed' — this schema is an evidence-track probe answer.

judgment_version.description: §6.1 ownership bullet's 'version' (the format version); the specification's own version is question.spec_version — the two are distinct, and §6's specification-version process governs the latter.

question.description: §6 'question identity and version' — a new question definition or changed decision semantics enters an explicit specification-version process (§6).

conventions.description: §6 'terms, units and temporal conventions'; §6.1 'terms, measurement units, EVIDENCE SOURCES, reference time, and time-window conventions' — explicit asset units and valuation, reference time, time-window boundaries (the credit example's named gaps).

reference_time.description: Which time a value is measured at — stated, not assumed.

time_window.description: The boundary convention of any window (e.g. inclusive/exclusive ends) — the 'past six months' gap the credit example names.

evidence_sources.description: §6.1 'terms, measurement units, evidence sources, reference time, and time-window conventions' — the sources a rule's facts come from, stated explicitly.

levels.description: §6 'level names, definitions and type'; current anchor: overall-design §5 — "The existing typed-readout research vocabulary includes boolean, nominal and ordinal levels".

candidate_set.description: §6 'candidate-set semantics'; current anchor: overall-design §5 — "…exclusive or stackable candidate sets".

rules.description: §6 'precedence, coverage and exception rules' — §6.1 'predicate boundaries, rule precedence, exclusions, and the scope of each condition'; the credit example's override rule is the precedence case.

precedence.description: Lower number wins — the explicit override order; equal precedence is a conflict the resolution section must name.

resolution.description: §6.1 'output states and the permitted action for each; missing evidence or an undefined rule is not automatically a negative business answer' — the actions must be stated, never defaulted to a denial.

examples.description: §6 'examples'; §6.1 'including boundaries, equivalent cases, competing rules, and unresolved cases' — the counterexample discipline.

scope.description: §6 'supported scope' — what this specification claims to cover.

ownership.description: Ownership and effective scope. Drift register: owner/review_authority/effective_scope/change_rationale/impacted_links trace to the legacy overall-design §6.1 ('ownership, review authority, version, effective scope, change rationale, and links to impacted tasks, datasets, and decisions'); the current proposal has no landing sentence for this family (knowledge-engineering boundary §2 names the responsibility but not the fields). Semantics load-bearing — retained per legacy provenance, awaiting upstream restoration (issue #1 collision response L2).

impacted_links.description: §6.1 'links to impacted tasks, datasets, and decisions' — what this specification's changes touch; accrues over revisions, so optional (a fresh v1 may impact nothing yet).
